record.paper_title: Twenty Open Questions in Supersymmetric Particle Physics
record.context_brief: Roles of SUSY in string theory
record.original_question: What roles does supersymmetry play in perturbative string theory, including the introduction of spacetime fermions through worldsheet supersymmetry, the relation between worldsheet and spacetime supersymmetry and the critical spacetime dimension, the possible stabilization of string vacua by cancelling dilaton tadpoles, and the resolution of pseudo-anomalous U(1) Fayet-Iliopoulos terms through vacuum shifting that can also generate intermediate mass scales?

evidence.quote: Question #18: What roles does SUSY play in string theory?
In order to introduce spacetime fermions, a natural idea is to supersymmetrize this worldsheet action, introducing superpartner fermionic fields ψµ(σ) on the worldsheet.
Spacetime supersymmetry is an elegant way of cancelling this dilaton tadpole.

What does this have to do with supersymmetry? It turns out that even though the anomalies caused by having Tr QX ≠ 0 are cancelled by the Green-Schwarz mechanism, there is still another danger: such a non-vanishing trace leads to the breaking of spacetime supersymmetry at one-loop order through the appearance of a one-loop Fayet-Iliopoulos D-term.
Vacuum shifting in string theory provides an economical mechanism for generating intermediate mass scales.

artifact.status_search_result: The component questions are largely understood at the level of perturbative string theory: the equivalence of RNS (with GSO projection) and Green–Schwarz formulations, the derivation of D=10/26 from conformal anomaly cancellation, the link between unbroken SUSY and vanishing dilaton tadpoles, and the one-loop FI-term computation by Dine–Seiberg–Witten and Atick–Dixon–Sen are classical results. However, the converse direction (non-SUSY vacua with vanishing tadpoles, stability of non-supersymmetric strings) and the full nonperturbative picture remain active research topics, so the overarching question is best described as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Anomalous U(1) and Fayet-Iliopoulos term in heterotic strings
status_evidence.snippet: Dine, Seiberg, Witten; Atick, Dixon, Sen computed the one-loop FI term proportional to Tr Q in anomalous-U(1) heterotic vacua and showed vacuum shifting restores SUSY.
status_evidence.claim: The FI-term and vacuum-shifting mechanism are established results.

status_evidence.title: GSO projection and spacetime supersymmetry
status_evidence.snippet: The GSO projection in the RNS superstring is required for modular invariance and produces a spacetime-supersymmetric spectrum in type II and heterotic theories.
status_evidence.claim: Worldsheet-to-spacetime SUSY link via GSO is standard.

status_evidence.title: Critical dimension of the superstring
status_evidence.snippet: Conformal anomaly cancellation fixes D=10 for the superstring and D=26 for the bosonic string.
